title: Isolation, Characterization and Mode of Action of a Plant-Derived Antifungal Peptide, Cc-AFP1 Against Aspergillus Fumigatus

materials_exhausted.note: Local recoverable material was exhausted for owner layers. PDF text and Research Square article HTML are the source-backed surfaces for curation; supplementary .bin files did not contain extra table data.

summary: Worker-2/4/6 source review repaired the empty activity layer, constrained database verification to the available literature row plus primary-source peptide evidence, and re-adjudicated mechanism as membrane permeability/damage. The paper is publication-grade only with cautions because a primary-source Cc-AFP1 sequence discrepancy and local source-artifact limitations remain explicit.
adjudication_summary: Source-reviewed worker-2/4/6 rework closed rwk-complete-test-0001 with accepted_with_cautions status: supported MIC/MFC/toxicity/mechanism values are recorded, no blocking rework remains, and unresolved sequence/source caveats are preserved as cautions.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: The single linked DBAASP literature record is source-verified for DOI/title/year. No linked sequence or assay rows are available; the primary-source Cc-AFP1 sequence discrepancy is preserved as source_conflict rather than normalized.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Worker-2 repaired the empty parser output by extracting PDF Table 1 MIC/MFC values for A. fumigatus Af293, A. flavus PFCC 100, and A. niger ATCC 9029, plus source-supported RDA and toxicity/hemolysis statements with explicit qualitative limits.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Worker-6 re-adjudicated direct mechanism evidence as membrane permeability/disruption supported by PI uptake and TEM, with in-silico/physicochemical features kept as supporting evidence only.
per_layer_decision_rationale.publication_decision: Accepted with cautions: no blocking or major rework target remains after source review, but the sequence conflict and source-artifact limitations must remain visible.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Primary source reports two different 36-aa Cc-AFP1 sequences: Edman/abstract sequence RVCFRPVATYLGVCGVSGACRDHCVKLGSCVYKGPG and Table 2 sequence RVCFRPVATYLGVCGVSGACRDRCVKLGSCVYKGPG. No linked sequence database row is locally available to resolve this.
XML-derived sections did not expose usable focused article sections/tables, so activity and mechanism repair used the local PDF text plus Research Square article HTML.
Packet supplementary .bin assets are HTML/support/privacy pages or article HTML, not recoverable spreadsheet/office/PDF supplementary tables.

closed_rework_tickets.resolution: worker-2 extracted supported activity/toxicity rows from PDF Table 1/results; worker-4 preserved sequence/database limits; worker-6 re-adjudicated final review and mechanism from source locators.

nonblocking_source_limitations.finding: The XML/derived xml_sections artifact is not a reliable focused article-section source for this DOI; the source-reviewed values were therefore taken from the paper PDF text and Research Square article HTML.
The three packet supplementary .bin assets are HTML pages, not local XLSX/DOCX/PDF supplementary data tables; no additional activity or toxicity tables were recoverable from them.

The packet contains one DBAASP linked literature row and zero linked sequence, assay, experiment, or DRAMP activity rows; database curation is therefore limited to DOI/title traceability plus primary-source peptide evidence.
